questions.title: Coffee Bean Roast
questions.prompt:
Create a class `CoffeeBean` in `CoffeeBean.java`:
* **Private fields:** `String origin`, `String roastLevel`, `int acidityScore`, `double bagPrice`.
* **Constructor 1:** `CoffeeBean(String origin, String roastLevel, int acidityScore, double bagPrice)`.
* **Constructor 2:** `CoffeeBean(String origin, String roastLevel)` which sets `acidityScore = 5` and `bagPrice = 14.99`.
* **Getters and Setters:** For all four fields.
  * In `setAcidityScore(int score)`: Must be between 1 and 10 inclusive. If `< 1`, set to `1`. If `> 10`, set to `10`.
  * In `setBagPrice(double price)`: If `price < 0.0`, set to `0.0`.

questions.prompt:

questions.title: Storage Vault Allocation
questions.prompt:
Create a checked exception `StorageQuotaExceededException` in `StorageQuotaExceededException.java` that extends `Exception` with a constructor taking `String message`.

In `CloudStorage.java`, implement:
`public static int allocateSpace(int currentUsedGB, int fileGB, int totalCapacityGB) throws StorageQuotaExceededException`
* If `fileGB <= 0`, throw `IllegalArgumentException` with message: `"File size must be positive"`.
* If `currentUsedGB + fileGB > totalCapacityGB`, throw `StorageQuotaExceededException` with message:
  `"Quota exceeded: required <currentUsedGB + fileGB>GB, capacity is <totalCapacityGB>GB"`.
* Otherwise, return `currentUsedGB + fileGB`.

Quota exceeded: required 105GB, capacity is 100GB

questions.title: Fitness Trackable
questions.prompt:
Create an interface `TrackableActivity` in `TrackableActivity.java`:
* Abstract method: `int getDurationMinutes();`
* Abstract method: `double getCaloriesPerMinute();`
* Default method: `default double calculateTotalCalories()`: returns `getDurationMinutes() * getCaloriesPerMinute()`.
* Default method: `default boolean reachedGoal(double goalCalories)`: returns `true` if `calculateTotalCalories() >= goalCalories`, else `false`.

Create a class `Running` in `Running.java` implementing `TrackableActivity`:
* **Private fields:** `int duration`, `double paceSpeedMPH`.
* **Constructor:** `Running(int duration, double paceSpeedMPH)`.

* Implement `getCaloriesPerMinute()`:
  * If `paceSpeedMPH >= 8.0`, burns `15.0` cal/min.
  * If `paceSpeedMPH >= 5.0`, burns `10.0` cal/min.
  * Otherwise burns `6.0` cal/min.

questions.title: Academic Course Enrollments
questions.prompt:

questions.title: Bank Account Statement Parser
questions.prompt:
In `StatementReader.java`, write:
`public static double computeNetCashFlow(String filename) throws FileNotFoundException`
* The file contains transactions per line: `TransactionID,Type,Amount`
  Example: `TX1001,DEPOSIT,250.50` or `TX1002,WITHDRAWAL,75.25`
* First line is a header (`ID,Type,Amount`) and must be skipped.
* For type `"DEPOSIT"`, add the amount to net cash flow.
* For type `"WITHDRAWAL"`, subtract the amount from net cash flow.
* Any other type should be ignored.
* If the file has no data rows, return `0.0`.
* If the file is missing, throw `FileNotFoundException`. Ensure file stream is closed.

questions.title: Inventory Expiration Tracker
questions.prompt:
This question gives you a question-specific abstract class **and** a question-specific interface. Your class must extend one and implement the other.

Create an abstract class `PerishableItem` in `PerishableItem.java`:
* **Protected fields:** `String batchId`, `String itemName`.
* **Constructor:** `PerishableItem(String batchId, String itemName)`.
* **Getters:** `getBatchId()`, `getItemName()`.
* **Abstract method:** `public abstract int daysUntilExpiry();` *(may be `0` or negative when already expired)*.

Create an interface `Expirable` in `Expirable.java`:
* Abstract method: `int shelfDaysLeft();`
* Default method: `default boolean isExpiring(int windowDays)`: returns `true` when `shelfDaysLeft() <= windowDays` (inclusive — already-expired items always count).
* Default method: `default boolean isExpired()`: returns `true` when `shelfDaysLeft() <= 0`.

Create a class `DairyBatch` in `DairyBatch.java` that **extends `PerishableItem` and implements `Expirable`**:
* **Private fields:** `int shelfLifeDays`, `int ageDays`.
* **Constructor:** `DairyBatch(String batchId, String itemName, int shelfLifeDays, int ageDays)` calling `super`.
* `daysUntilExpiry()` returns `shelfLifeDays - ageDays` (this can be negative).
* `shelfDaysLeft()` must return the same value as `daysUntilExpiry()`.

*Edge cases to think about (not in the sample): the expiring window is inclusive; `0` days left means expired; a negative value (already spoiled) is both expired and expiring; a fresh item is neither.*
questions.expectedOutput:
Days until expiry: 3
Expiring within 7: true
Expired: false

tests.description: Days-until-expiry, inclusive expiring window, and not-yet-expired.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Expiring Window Inclusive)
tests.description: isExpiring is true at exactly the window and false just below it.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Zero Days Left)
tests.description: 0 days left counts as both expired and expiring.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Already Expired Negative)
tests.description: A negative days-until-expiry is expired and always expiring.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Fresh Item)
tests.description: A fresh item is neither expired nor expiring in a short window.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Polymorphic Dispatch)
tests.description: daysUntilExpiry invoked through a PerishableItem reference.

tests.name: Test 7 [Hidden] (Type Contracts)
tests.description: DairyBatch is both a PerishableItem and an Expirable.

questions.title: Cloud Compute Hierarchy
questions.prompt:
This question requires a question-specific abstract class **and** a question-specific interface. Every concrete instance type must extend the class and implement the interface.

Create an abstract class `CloudInstance` in `CloudInstance.java`:
* **Protected fields:** `String instanceId`, `double baseHourlyRate`.
* **Constructor:** `CloudInstance(String instanceId, double baseHourlyRate)`.
* **Abstract method:** `public abstract double computeCost(double hoursRunning);`

Create an interface `Billable` in `Billable.java`:
* Abstract method: `double costFor(double hours);`
* Default method: `default double dailyEstimate()`: returns `costFor(24.0)`.
* Default method: `default boolean exceedsBudget(double hours, double budget)`: returns `true` when `costFor(hours)` is **strictly greater** than `budget`.

Create `OnDemandInstance` in `OnDemandInstance.java` **extending `CloudInstance` and implementing `Billable`**:
* **Constructor:** `OnDemandInstance(String instanceId, double baseHourlyRate)`.
* `computeCost(double hoursRunning)`: `baseHourlyRate * hoursRunning`.
* `costFor(double hours)` must return the same value as `computeCost(hours)`.

Create `SpotInstance` in `SpotInstance.java` **extending `CloudInstance` and implementing `Billable`**:
* **Private field:** `double bidDiscountPercent` (e.g. `60.0` for 60% off).
* **Constructor:** `SpotInstance(String instanceId, double baseHourlyRate, double bidDiscountPercent)` using `super`.
* `computeCost(double hoursRunning)`:
  * `effectiveRate = baseHourlyRate * (1.0 - (bidDiscountPercent / 100.0))`.
  * Base cost is `effectiveRate * hoursRunning`.
  * If `hoursRunning > 24.0`, subtract a `$2.00` interruption-risk rebate; the final cost **cannot drop below `0.0`**.
* `costFor(double hours)` must return the same value as `computeCost(hours)`.

*Edge cases to think about (not in the sample): `24.0` hours exactly gets no rebate but `24.1` does; the rebate cannot push cost negative; a 100% discount is free; `exceedsBudget` is strict at the budget.*

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: On-demand linear rate, spot 50% discount, spot > 24h rebate.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Spot Exact 24 Hours)
tests.description: 24.0 hours does NOT receive the $2.00 rebate.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Spot 24.1 Hours)
tests.description: Just over 24 hours receives the $2.00 rebate.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Spot Zero Floor)
tests.description: Spot cost cannot drop below 0.0 even after rebate.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (0 Hours Running)
tests.description: 0 hours running returns 0.0 for both types.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (100% Discount Spot)
tests.description: 100% discount spot costs 0.0.

tests.name: Test 7 [Hidden] (Billable Defaults)
tests.description: dailyEstimate uses costFor(24) and exceedsBudget is strict at the budget.

graderCases.name: Sample run (on-demand, spot discount, >24h rebate + types)
Spot exactly 24 hours: no rebate
graderCases.body:
SpotInstance s = new SpotInstance("x",2.00,50.0);
eqD(s.computeCost(24.0),24.0);

graderCases.name: Spot just over 24 hours: rebate applies
graderCases.body:

eqD(s.computeCost(25.0),23.0);

graderCases.name: Spot cost floored at 0.0
graderCases.body:

eqD(s.computeCost(25.0),0.0);

graderCases.name: Zero hours returns 0.0 for both
graderCases.body:

eqD(new SpotInstance("b",3.0,10.0).computeCost(0.0),0.0);

questions.title: Smart Greenhouse Controller
questions.prompt:
This capstone requires a question-specific abstract class **and** a question-specific interface, extended/implemented together by your concrete class.

Create an abstract class `Greenhouse` in `Greenhouse.java`:
* **Protected fields:** `String zoneId`, `int temp`, `int water`.
* **Constructor:** `Greenhouse(String zoneId, int startTemp, int startWater)`.
* **Getters:** `getTemp()`, `getWater()`.
* Method `heat(int degrees)`: raise `temp` by `degrees`.
* **Abstract method:** `public abstract boolean mist();`

Create an interface `ClimateControlled` in `ClimateControlled.java`:
* Abstract methods: `int currentTemp();`, `int safeLow();`, `int safeHigh();`
* Default method: `default boolean inSafeRange()`: `true` only when `currentTemp()` is **strictly between** `safeLow()` and `safeHigh()` (the thresholds themselves are emergencies).
* Default method: `default boolean freezeAlert()`: `true` when `currentTemp() <= safeLow()`.
* Default method: `default boolean heatAlert()`: `true` when `currentTemp() >= safeHigh()`.

Create a class `TomatoGreenhouse` in `TomatoGreenhouse.java` that **extends `Greenhouse` and implements `ClimateControlled`**:
* **Constructor:** `TomatoGreenhouse(String zoneId, int startTemp, int startWater)` calling `super`.
* `mist()`: if `water < 10`, **refuse** — return `false` and change nothing. Otherwise deduct `10` gal, drop `temp` by `5`, and return `true`.
* `currentTemp()` returns the current temperature.
* `safeLow()` returns `45`; `safeHigh()` returns `95`.

*Edge cases to think about (not in the sample): misting is refused (no state change) when the reserve is under 10; misting with exactly 10 gal depletes to 0; `45` and `95` are emergency boundaries, NOT safe; `inSafeRange` is strict.*
questions.expectedOutput:
Temp: 76F | Water: 50 gal
Temp: 71F | Water: 40 gal
In safe range: true

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: Heat lamps raise temp, misting cools and uses water, temperature stays in the safe band.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Mist Refused Under 10 gal)
tests.description: A refused mist returns false and leaves temp and water unchanged.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Mist Exactly 10 gal)
tests.description: Misting with exactly 10 gal succeeds and depletes water to 0.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Freeze Boundary at 45)
tests.description: At exactly 45F the freeze alert fires and the zone is NOT in safe range.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Heat Boundary at 95)
tests.description: At exactly 95F the heat alert fires and the zone is NOT in safe range.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Strict Safe Range)
tests.description: A temperature strictly inside the band is safe with no alerts.

tests.name: Test 7 [Hidden] (Heat Into Alert)
tests.description: Heating up to the safe high triggers the heat alert.

Temp: 71F | Water: 40 gal
In safe range: true
